text:
anya: heads up — we just got an alert: fncall schema rejects spiked to ~8% for the payments flow, started ~5m ago. sample attached in logs.

deploy-bot: alert: metric fncall.reject_rate{svc=payments} = 0.08 (5m avg) — threshold breached.

ben: thanks — do we have breakdown by reject reason? is this validation vs parse error vs unexpected-type?

anya: quick grok from logs: mostly "missing_required_field" and a chunk of "unexpected_array_instead_of_object". payload size similar to normal.

chao: probable culprit: the new invoice consolidation change in serving-runtime that added `line_items` as optional object. some older model outputs still emit arrays.

linda: is this user-facing? any customer impact?

anya: some downstream routes are falling back to the general LLM model because strict fncall validation rejects, so latency increased for a tiny slice and quota billing hit fallback rate. No P0 yet but noisy.

ben: console telemetry currently only surfaces fncall.reject_rate as a single metric. we should break it down by: reason, model_variant, route, and whether it triggered fallback routing. query I'd add: `sum(rate(fncall.rejects[5m])) by (reason, model_variant, route, triggered_fallback)`

chao: agree. Also need to differentiate between "soft_validate" (we mark but allow) vs "hard_reject" (we abort). right now both increment the same counter.

anya: short-term mitigation: can we stop counting soft_validate as rejects for quota/fallback decisions? make them advisory only.

chao: yes, we can flip behavior in routing policy: only treat hard_rejects as capacity failure that triggers fallback. will push small change. patch will be behind a canary flag `fncall.strict_counting=false`.

linda: UX ask: product wants the console to show both counts and an example redacted payload for the top N offending samples so customers can debug. also surface reason percentages next to the metric sparkline.

ben: for sampling — currently we sample 1% of rejects for payload capture. bump to 5% for the next 30min window for payments tenants. add deterministic sampling by route+day so we get reproducible examples.

anya: sounds good. for the immediate rollout: 1) flip routing policy behavior behind canary 2) add reason tag to metrics/traces 3) increase sampling 4) dashboard tile update. owners?

chao: i'll own (1) and (2). I'll open a PR for the canary and the metric label change. estimated 2h to review.

ben: i'll own (3) and (4) — update alerts and the dashboard panel. ben -> PR to grafana and alerts.

linda: i'll draft a short customer note for impacted customers and a console blurb explaining why fallback may have occurred.

anya: for observability: please make sure traces link to the exact request id and show the validation diff. e.g., in trace span add `validation.diff = "expected.line_items:object vs got:array"` so SREs can triage faster.

chao: good call. i'll also emit a counter `fncall.validation_diff_seen{diff_hash=...}` so we can aggregate similar diffs without leaking payloads.

ben: privacy check: double-check payload redaction policy before exposing samples. we only ship hashed user identifiers and redact account numbers.

anya: agreed — redaction library will run before storing samples. policy: remove keys matching /(ssn|card|acct|account_number)/i and hash emails/user ids.

linda: timeline? we want the canary ASAP and dashboard within the hour.

chao: canary PR in 30m, deploy to canary env in 45m. If stable, flip for payments route after 1h.

ben: I'll update the dashboard PR in 40m and increase sampling via the feature flag targeting payments tenants.

anya: postmortem/notes: add a short section to the incidents backlog describing this as a schema-compat regression between runtime changes and model variants. suggest adding a periodic synthetic check that validates model outputs against current schema for critical flows.

linda: pls add that to product backlog. also make sure downstream saga handlers gracefully accept both array and object for backward compat.

chao: small follow-up: should we change quota accounting? currently fallback requests are billed at premium. we should not bill customers extra if fallback triggered by our validation bug. create a billing exemption tag `billing.exempt_reason=fncall_runtime_validation` for affected window.

anya: yes — ops/finance will need a list of request ids and time window. I'll assemble that after canary stabilizes.

ben: one more: add a low-traffic canary alert that watches `fncall.reject_rate` per-route with a 15m window and a relaxation threshold so we don't noise SRE. rule: fire if >3% sustained for 15m and increase by >2x from baseline.

anya: perfect. thanks everyone. I'll update the thread with PR links once they're up.

chao: PRs: runtime change https://git.company/repo/pull/4321 (draft) — includes canary flag and metric label.

ben: dashboard PR https://grafana.company/d/xyz/fncall-health?orgId=1 (diff in panel 3). I'll post the alert rule after tests.

linda: customer note draft posted in #customer-comm: https://docs.company/notes/incident-fncall-2943210000 — feedback welcome.

anya: leaving this open until we verify post-canary. tagging owners: @chao @ben @linda.

deploy-bot: deployment to canary succeeded: runtime-v2.14-canary @ 2943210245

chao: canary looks clean at +20m, reject rate down to 1.2% and fallback traffic normalized. will keep running for 1h then propose flip.

ben: sampling capture shows 12 redacted examples; uploading to secure store for ops.

linda: sending customer note to impacted tenants now.

anya: great work — we'll close after 1h stable and create follow-up ticket for synthetic schema checks and billing exemptions.

chao: creating follow-up: INC-2943211 (action items + synthetic checks).

ben: closing loop: alert thresholds updated and dashboard panel merged.

anya: thread closed once billing exemption completes. thanks all.
